C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE.Summary: Make `ngrace cursor recover --fix` produce a ledger that can actually fold: close F13 (covering allocation with no headroom for a later terminal) and repair the already-damaged live shape on C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY, without deleting the NaN orphan. Completes the fold half of C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY's AC-RECOVER-FIX-PRESERVES-ORPHAN (F13.1); C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY and C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY remain unarchivable until this lands.
C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE.Problem:
C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY shipped `cursor recover` so a corrupt run ledger can be repaired and folded without `rm -r run/`. On the real artifact that motivated the command, the fold half of that promise does not hold.
F13. `writeCoveringOpened` (grace-cursor.ts:736–751) sets `to = Math.max(options.to, openedId)`, so the covering allocation's ceiling is the covering event's own id. Fold requires a `kind=terminal` event *inside* some allocation (`validateEventsAgainstAllocations:2475–2478`). The terminal is correctly an operator act (F12 / A29.2) and can only be written *after* the fix — so it always lands outside the new allocation. Validation loops **per allocation**, so a second covering opened does not rescue the first: the dead allocation stays unterminated forever. Reproduced:
fix #1 → w0:[1,4] blocked: unterminated range for w0 terminal at id 5 → outside [1,4] fix #2 → w0:[1,4], w0:[1,6] still blocked: unterminated range for w0
Therefore `recover --fix` cannot produce a foldable ledger on any bundle that does not already contain a terminal inside its pre-fix id range. C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY itself is foldable only by luck: its epoch was opened with the CLI default to=from+98, so terminal id 33 sits inside w0:[1,99].
F13.1 / F12.1. The acceptance test that claimed "fold succeeds" seeded `seedF8Shape(..., { withTerminal: true })`, placing a terminal *inside* the pre-fix valid id set — the one precondition the feature cannot establish for itself. The orphan-survival half of AC-RECOVER-FIX-PRESERVES-ORPHAN holds on the real ledger and is verified. The fold half does not. C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY is therefore not complete and must not archive until this repair lands.
Live damage. C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/ is already worse than the pre-fix F8 shape. Current diagnosis (authoritative snapshot for this bundle):
Orphans: 1 — NaN-T-001-opened.xml [event-filename] unrecoverable Loose integer events: 1..20 (count=20) Valid covering allocation: missing (w0:1-19) Fold: blocked (event 20 outside every allocation; unterminated range for w0) Workers: w0
There is a **dead allocation** w0:[1,19] written by the first `--fix`, containing no terminal and incapable of ever containing one (the terminal is event 20, outside it). A design that only changes what *future* covering allocations look like leaves this ledger permanently unfoldable. The NaN orphan (SHA-1 c0cc8899c264381766a18918e2109b5e05693893) must still survive every repair (D8.3 / F8.1).
Flag honesty. `--fix` is documented as `extend-allocation` (grace-cursor.ts:3221) and never extends anything — it always writes a new covering opened. A flag whose name asserts behaviour it does not have is the same class of defect this track addresses.
Sequencing (F13.2). C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY cannot fold until this lands; C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY cannot archive until its own AC holds. Approved C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY plan is immutable with eight complete tasks and no room for a ninth — same precedent as F10 → F10.2 (repair in the next bundle with a recorded sequential ObservedWriteScope overlap).

Goals.Goal: After recover --fix on a clean shape with no terminal anywhere, an operator-emitted terminal, and fold, the epoch folds successfully and any unrecoverable orphan survives on disk and in diagnosis (F13 property; D8.3).

Repair the already-damaged live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY shape (dead allocation w0:[1,19], terminal at 20 outside every allocation, NaN orphan present) so the ledger becomes foldable, folds, and keeps the orphan present and diagnosed — not merely prevent the defect on new ledgers.
Align the --fix operation with its documented name: either the operation extends an allocation, or the documented name says what the operation does (flag honesty).
Replace the withTerminal-seeded "fold succeeds" demonstration with end-to-end regressions that do not supply a pre-fix terminal (F12.1 / F13.1).

Constraints.Constraint: Binding decisions and findings: D8.2, D8.3, A29.2 / F1, F8.1, F10.2 (overlap precedent), F12, F12.1, F13, F13.1, F13.2. Emitting a terminal remains the operator's act — it asserts the work is finished, which is a judgment, not structural state the binary can derive. recover --fix must not emit a terminal.

A29.2 — the binary writes only structural state it can derive or is explicitly given, never authored content, and never without an explicit apply. Covering-allocation bounds remain derived from inventory (or explicitly given by the operator); the operator act is the --fix (or equivalent) command. Forbidden: inventing an id for a NaN orphan, fabricating multi-worker partitions, rewriting attempt outcomes, deleting run/ events or the orphan, or hand-editing Allocation attributes outside the recorded recover path.

Sequential ObservedWriteScope overlap with C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY on src/grace-cursor.ts and src/grace-cursor.test.ts, authorized under F10.2 precedent and F13.2 disposition. C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY is code-complete (all eight tasks landed); nothing will write those files under that bundle again — the overlap is sequential, not concurrent. Still out of this bundle: every other path in C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY's write scope (src/grace-status.ts|.test.ts, src/review/*, src/lint/catalog.test.ts) and that bundle's plan/spec. Expect ngrace lint to report a second scope.durable-overlap warning once this bundle's plan is approved; that warning is correct and must not be suppressed (F10.2 / F10.3).

Do not mutate the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY or C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY ledgers as part of implementing this bundle. Those ledgers are evidence. Tests exercise copies of the clean no-terminal shape and of the damaged shape. Applying the repair to the real C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/ is a separate authorized act by the authority after this lands — not an implementation task of this change.

Spec only in this authoring pass (F4 two-stage authoring). status remains "draft"; approval is a human act. Do not author plan.xml until the spec is approved (grammar.ts forbids an active plan beside a non-approved spec). Do not hand-edit CHANGELOG.md (D5.5).

Evidence doctrine: TraceAssertion + tests default. Write each regression first, watch it fail on pre-fix code, then fix. Do not seed withTerminal: true to satisfy the fold-succeeds property under test.

NonGoals.NonGoal: P0.8 calibration backfill / command-run evidence adjudication, any edit under src/calibration/, or fold-time CalibrationAdjudication redesign (D8.1).

Everything else in C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY's ObservedWriteScope beyond grace-cursor: src/grace-status.ts|.test.ts, src/review/core.ts|.test.ts, src/review/catalog.ts, src/lint/catalog.test.ts, and that bundle's plan/spec.
The ngrace-execute documentation gap from F12 (terminal never mentioned in SKILL.md). That goes to P1 (authoring/execution surface / RC-4), not this repair.
Re-litigating F9.3's weakened attempt-pair rule, inventing finding-clearance ledger schema, or reopening C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY's approved plan to add a ninth task (approved plans are immutable; F13.2).

Deleting, renaming, or hand-editing C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/NaN-T-001-opened.xml or any event under that bundle's run/ as part of this change. Hand-editing a dead Allocation attribute outside the recover path is also out of scope.
Making fold accept an unterminated range, or having recover --fix emit a terminal on the operator's behalf (F12 / A29.2).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECOVER-FIX-FOLDABLE-CLEAN: Given a run/ with loose integer events, no valid covering allocation, and **no terminal event anywhere** (including no withTerminal seed), after `recover --fix`, an operator-emitted `cursor advance --kind terminal`, and `cursor fold`, the epoch **folds successfully**. Any unrecoverable orphan present before the sequence still exists on disk afterward and is still reported by `recover` as an unrecoverable orphan. A design that only prevents the defect on new ledgers but cannot complete this clean-shape sequence fails this criterion. Mechanism (allocation headroom, in-place extend, or validation change) is left to the plan; the property is binding.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECOVER-FIX-DAMAGED-SHAPE: Given a **copy** of C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY's **current** ledger shape — loose integer events 1..20, a dead allocation w0:[1,19] with no terminal in range (as written by the first recover --fix), a terminal at id 20 outside every allocation, and the NaN-* orphan (event-filename class, SHA-1 of the live fixture c0cc8899c264381766a18918e2109b5e05693893) — the ledger becomes foldable under the designated recover path, and folds, with the orphan still present on disk and still diagnosed as an unrecoverable orphan. **A design which repairs clean shapes but leaves an existing dead allocation unfoldable fails this criterion.** Preventing the defect on future covering allocations alone is not sufficient: the real artifact already carries a dead allocation and is the subject this criterion judges against. Tests must exercise a copy; they must not mutate the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FIX-FLAG-HONESTY: The --fix operation and its documented name agree. Today --fix is documented as `extend-allocation` (grace-cursor.ts:3221 / help text) and always writes a new covering opened without extending any existing Allocation. After this change, either (1) the operation actually extends an existing covering allocation when one is present and incomplete (matching the name), or (2) the documented name and help text describe what the operation does (e.g. create-covering) and no longer claim "extend". A criterion or implementation that leaves the name asserting behaviour the code does not perform fails this criterion. Which alternative is the plan's choice; agreement is binding.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REGRESSION-NO-PRESEEDED-TERMINAL: End-to-end regression coverage includes: (1) the clean shape of AC-RECOVER-FIX-FOLDABLE-CLEAN (no terminal anywhere before --fix), fixed, operator-terminated, folded; (2) the damaged-shape repair of AC-RECOVER-FIX-DAMAGED-SHAPE. **Neither may be satisfied by seeding `withTerminal: true` (or equivalent)** — that option supplies the precondition under test and is the exact fixture defect of F12.1 / F13.1. A test that passes only because a terminal was present inside the pre-fix id range does not satisfy this criterion. Prior AC-RECOVER-FIX-PRESERVES-ORPHAN orphan-survival assertions remain; the fold-succeeds half is proven by the new no-preseeded-terminal paths.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CARRIED-ORPHAN-WORKER-A29: Carried constraints, not reopened: (D8.3) recover never deletes unrecoverable orphans; NaN-* stays on disk and diagnosed after --fix and after fold of the valid stream. (D8.2) when more than one distinct worker value appears in ledger∪loose Allocations, recover --fix and auto-open refuse; multi-worker ranges are never fabricated. (A29.2 / F12) recover --fix does not emit a terminal; the operator emits the terminal; the binary writes only structural state it can derive or is explicitly given, with --fix as the explicit apply for the covering allocation path. A change that violates any of these to make fold succeed fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-LINT: Suite green for the new regressions and retained recover/orphan/auto-open coverage; bun run validate:ci and bun run ngrace lint --path . are green on this repository (0 errors; scope.durable-overlap warnings against C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY and any continuing C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY overlap are expected and authorized — F10.2 / F10.3 — and must not be suppressed).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit and CLI regressions under src/grace-cursor.test.ts that fail before the fix and pass after: clean no-terminal fix→terminal→fold; damaged-shape copy of C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY current run/ (dead w0:[1,19], terminal at 20, NaN orphan) repaired and folded with orphan survival; flag-name/docs agreement with behaviour; multi-worker refuse retained; orphan never deleted. Dogfooding ngrace lint --path . at 0 errors (authorized scope.durable-overlap warnings only). TraceAssertion-backed V-M-CURSOR as already declared; no new Marker evidence.

Assumptions.Assumption: Module ownership confirmed against .ngrace/graph/main.xml: M-CURSOR Path src/grace-cursor.ts (ENTRY_POINT). V-M-CURSOR in .ngrace/verification/main.xml runs bun test src/grace-cursor.test.ts. No invented module ids. grace-cursor.test.ts is the co-located test for M-CURSOR (same pattern as other ENTRY_POINT modules).

F13 / F13.1 / F13.2 and F12 / F12.1 in docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md are authoritative for this bundle's under-specifications. C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY AC-RECOVER-FIX-PRESERVES-ORPHAN's fold-succeeds clause is the debt this bundle retires; that plan is not edited.

Live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY diagnosis at authoring (HEAD 585598a family): loose events 1..20, allocation w0:[1,19] on 19-T-005-opened.xml, terminal 20-T-005-terminal.xml outside that range, NaN-T-001-opened.xml with SHA-1 c0cc8899c264381766a18918e2109b5e05693893, workers w0 only. If the live ledger moves before implementation, AC-RECOVER-FIX-DAMAGED-SHAPE still targets that *shape* (dead closed-ceiling allocation + terminal outside + NaN orphan), not a particular commit's byte-for-byte tree beyond the orphan's fixed SHA.

Mechanism is intentionally unspecified in this spec (authority decision §4 A): allocation headroom on the covering opened, in-place extend of an existing Allocation, a validation change that still requires a terminal inside some covering range, or another design that satisfies the properties. The plan chooses; the criteria judge outcomes on clean and damaged shapes.

Applying the repair to the *live* C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY run/ (and folding both blocked bundles) remains a separate mechanical act by the authority after this change lands — same separation as C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY's constraint that implementers do not --fix the live fixture during development. This bundle's tests use copies only.

C-CURSOR-INTEGRITY remains active and code-complete; its epoch is currently foldable (Fold: ok after terminal 33 inside w0:[1,99]) but archive waits on this AC. Concurrent writes under that bundle to grace-cursor.ts are not expected (F10.2 sequential-overlap premise).

If implementation discovers that making a dead prior allocation foldable requires rewriting historical Allocation attributes on an existing opened event (rather than a new ledger-visible recover event), stop and report: whether in-place mutation of a prior event is permitted under A29.2 / audit immutability is the authority's call, not the implementer's.
